jobs.description:
About the Team
Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role
We are seeking a senior Global Security Investigator with a technical background to lead complex, long-running security investigations involving a full spectrum of threats – whether originating from internal employees, external threat actors, or supply chain partners. This role is about seeing the full chessboard and independently driving complex, multi-month cases across cyber, physical, and human domains.

In this role you will:
• Independently conduct comprehensive security investigations from initial detection to resolution, including cases involving insiders, external actors, and supply chain and third-party risks.

• Lead proactive, data-driven threat-hunting efforts that weave together disparate signals to surface undetected insider or external threats before they escalate into incidents.

• Perform comprehensive technical analysis of complex hardware, software, and supplier supply chains to identify, enumerate, and mitigate risks.

• Partner closely with cross-functional teams, including Human Resources, Legal, Security, and IT, and external stakeholders or law enforcement when necessary.

• Collaborate with technical counterparts to enhance detections, resolve telemetry gaps, and implement new capabilities to identify security issues involving cyber, physical, and human domains.

• Collect, preserve, and analyze evidence from a variety of sources, including log data, digital forensics, subject interviews, access records, threat intelligence, and open-source intelligence (OSINT), to support investigative findings.

• Continuously improve investigative procedures and security controls based on investigations and lessons learned.

You might thrive in this role if you have:
• Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Cybersecurity, or a related field (or equivalent experience) and 8+ years of investigative experience in counterintelligence, insider risk, forensic investigations, cybersecurity, supply chain security, or related domains.

• Unimpeachable integrity, sound judgment, and the ability to handle confidential matters with discretion.

• An active US security clearance, or willingness and eligibility to obtain one.

• Deep specialization in geopolitical threat domains, with hands-on experience identifying, assessing, and mitigating adversarial risks through tailored countermeasures.

• Expert knowledge of common security tooling, including EDR, DLP, UEBA, SIEM, SOAR and other related platforms.

• Demonstrated ability to independently write complex queries, automate data workflows, and analyze structured datasets.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex findings into clear, actionable reports and explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders.

• Exceptional collaboration skills with the ability to work across diverse teams (HR, Legal, IT, etc.) to lead projects and investigations with minimal guidance.

About OpenAI
OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.
For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement .

jobs.description:
Manager, Corporate Security – New York City (HQ) based

The Global Safety & Security Team falls under the Operations team that runs many day-to-day operational functions that help keep our employees safe, happy and productive. We work closely with leadership and employees to ensure that Datadog continues to scale rapidly, yet smoothly and remains a fantastic place to work.

We’re seeking an experienced team member to join our growing global team and play a critical role in keeping Datadogs and our assets safe and secure. You will work directly with the Global Safety & Security Sr Manager - AMER and cross-functional teams to support safety and security operations across the enterprise. Ideal candidates will be passionate about security operations, program development, leadership, project management, customer service and collaboration.

This position is based in our New York City headquarters and may require occasional domestic and international travel. The role will focus particularly on three core pillars: Headquarters Security, Global Security Operations Center operations and occasional management of the executive protection program

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. This position requires being in-office 5 days a week.

What You’ll Do:

Headquarters Security:

• Manage daily safety and security operations at Datadog’s New York City headquarters, including contract security personnel, access control, visitor management, internal events and incident response.

• Oversee contract security personnel and vendors, including staffing, training, post orders, service levels, performance reviews and corrective actions. while maintaining a safe, professional and welcoming employee experience.

• Coordinate with building management, property security and internal teams to coordinate lobby operations, emergency response, life-safety matters and headquarters security incidents..

• Identify and address risks associated with operating in a high-profile urban environment, including protests, demonstrations, workplace violence, suspicious activity, property crime and other incidents that may affect Datadogs, visitors or business operations.

• Develop Security risk mitigation strategies. Support the implementation and management of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management and other technical security systems.

Global Security Operations Center:

• Advance Datadog’s GSOC as its central hub for global security monitoring, incident intake, triage, escalation, communication and response coordination.

• Develop and maintain GSOC standard operating procedures, escalation protocols, incident classifications, notification requirements, service levels and quality standards to ensure consistent global operations.

• Oversee resources supporting GSOC operations, including staffing, training, performance management, vendor relationships and operational readiness.

• Monitor global events, emerging threats and incidents that could affect Datadog’s employees, offices, executives, travelers, events or operations. Ensure timely and accurate communication during critical incidents, including security alerts, situation reports, leadership briefings and updates to impacted teams.

• Review incident trends, performance metrics and recurring risks to identify opportunities to improve processes, tools and response capabilities. Lead post-incident reviews and track corrective actions through completion.

Executive Protection:

• Manage and advance Datadog’s executive protection program, including protective intelligence, executive threat monitoring, travel and event security and response to identified or emerging threats.

• Partner with executives, executive assistants and internal stakeholders to provide security support that is discreet, practical and aligned with Datadog’s culture and business needs when necessary.

• Manage vendors, ensuring that providers meet Datadog’s expectations for professionalism, confidentiality, service and operational performance.

Who You Are:

• Experienced in managing corporate safety and security operations, ideally within a fast-paced technology environment, with a focus on headquarters security, GSOC operations and executive protection.

• Skilled in managing all aspects of a physical security program, including contract security personnel, access control, video surveillance, visitor management, event security, investigations and emergency response.

• Experienced in developing or managing a GSOC, security operations center, command center or similar 24/7 monitoring and incident response capability.

• Knowledgeable about GSOC operating standards, including incident intake, triage, escalation, communications, reporting, service levels, performance metrics and after-action reviews.

• Experienced in executive protection program management, including protective intelligence, threat monitoring, executive travel, advance planning, event security and third-party provider management.

• Able to assess complex or incomplete information, make sound decisions under pressure and communicate clear recommendations during sensitive or rapidly evolving situations.

• Experienced in conducting physical security and threat assessments, identifying vulnerabilities and developing proportionate mitigation strategies.

• Knowledgeable about workplace violence prevention, behavioral threat assessment, insider threat, crisis management and active assailant preparedness.

• Experienced with open-source intelligence, protective intelligence and threat-monitoring tools used to identify and evaluate potential risks involving employees, executives, facilities and business operations.

• Knowledgeable about technical security systems, with experience supporting physical security design and reviewing access control, surveillance, visitor management and intrusion detection solutions.

• An exceptional written and verbal communicator who can effectively convey security information across all levels of the organization, with a specific focus on executives and senior leadership.

• A strong cross-functional partner who can build trusted relationships with internal teams, building management, law enforcement, emergency services, peer organizations and external security providers.

• Experienced in building and growing safety and security programs that can scale with organizational needs while maintaining a strong employee and customer service focus.

• Able to exercise a high level of integrity, discretion and confidentiality when managing sensitive incidents, investigations and executive-related matters.

• Comfortable managing multiple priorities and operating with autonomy in a dynamic environment where risks, business needs and operational requirements may change quickly.

• 8+ years of progressively responsible experience in corporate security, physical security, GSOC operations, executive protection, law enforcement, intelligence, military security or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience managing contract security personnel or external security teams

• Able and willing to travel domestically and internationally and participate in an after-hours on-call rotation.

• Professional certifications or specialized training in corporate security, executive protection, threat assessment, emergency management or business continuity are preferred.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. Learn more about #DatadogLife on Instagram , LinkedIn, and Datadog Learning Center.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

About Global Affairs at Okta:

Okta’s Global Affairs organization is a newly consolidated, highly strategic function designed to drive business growth, navigate and shape regulatory landscapes, and advance our mission to build a more secure, inclusive, and sustainable world. Reporting directly to the Chief Legal Officer, this unified Global Affairs team brings together Government Affairs, Sustainability & Responsible Technology, and Social Impact & Nonprofit Go-To-Market (Okta for Good).

We operate at the critical intersection of public policy, trust, commercial strategy, and social good. Together, this team ensures Okta meets and promotes rigorous AI governance, sustainability, and compliance requirements of our largest enterprise and public sector customers, while advocating for public policy that advances Okta’s business and maintaining Okta’s strong brand reputation and cultural impact.

Role Overview:

We are seeking a Vice President of Global Affairs: a commercially-minded executive with a strong background in government affairs and public policy, coupled with a demonstrated ability to champion a corporate impact function. The ideal candidate is a strategic operator, a compelling storyteller, passionate about technology’s ability to lift communities, and a seasoned leader capable of navigating complex ecosystems—from public sector leaders and regulators to enterprise customers and global nonprofit partners.

This leader will report directly to the Chief Legal Officer and serve as a vital bridge between Okta’s legal and compliance frameworks, our responsible stewardship programs and our Go-To-Market (GTM) machinery. You will provide executive-level air cover for our durable business growth and success while relying on highly seasoned, domain-expert leaders to run the day-to-day operations of the team. You will be a thoughtful, courageous and publicly vocal proponent of Okta’s Global Affairs efforts.

This leader will oversee three critical pillars of Okta's business:

Government Affairs & Public Sector Growth

• Lead Okta’s global Government Affairs strategy, navigating and shaping regulatory environments and advancing Okta’s public policy priorities through thought leadership and advocacy.

• Partner directly with Okta’s GTM and public sector sales leaders to accelerate pipeline and unlock new commercial opportunities.

• Help expand Okta’s thought leadership in critical technology domains, helping us fulfill our vision to free everyone to safely use any technology.

• Expand the capacity and reach of the Government Affairs function by leveraging cross-trained talent across the Global Affairs organization.

Sustainability & Responsible Technology

• Oversee Okta’s sustainability strategy, disclosures, and compliance with escalating customer and regulatory requirements (including protecting and accelerating deal flow).

• Drive the successful reset and Board approval of Okta’s Science-Based Targets for emissions reductions.

• Champion a robust, centralized Responsible AI governance program across the business and our customers.

Social Impact & Okta for Good

• Oversee Okta’s nonprofit business and product donation commitment, partnering with GTM to drive growth while balancing social impact.

• Oversee Okta’s donor-advised fund, including the execution of our current $50M philanthropic commitment and the development of a future funding strategy.

• Champion Okta’s award-winning culture of giving, sustaining high employee engagement and brand value.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership

• Set a unified, bold strategy for Global Affairs that directly supports Okta’s commercial growth in large enterprise and public sector markets.

• Serve as an executive champion for trust, responsible AI, and mission-aligned growth.

• Represent Okta with senior external stakeholders, including government officials, regulators, enterprise customers, nonprofit partners, and investors.

• Present vision and operations to employees, executives and board members on an ongoing basis.

Go-To-Market (GTM) Integration

• Operate a powerful overlay model across GTM to drive revenue via Okta’s compliance readiness, sustainability commitments, and nonprofit product offerings.

• Ensure Okta is positioned as a trusted partner to the public sector and our most highly regulated customers.

Operational Excellence & Team Leadership

• Manage and develop a high-performing leadership team acting as a leader and champion of leaders.

• Foster a culture of cross-pollination, allowing team members to expand their domain expertise across government affairs, ESG, and social impact.

• Strengthen cross-functional relationships with GTM, Sales, Product, Marketing, Security, and the broader Legal organization.

What We’re Looking For:

Experience and Technical Expertise

• 15+ years of experience spanning Government Affairs, Public Policy, Global Affairs, Social Impact, and/or Corporate Strategy.

• Strong, demonstrated background in Government Affairs and public sector engagement is required.

• Executive-level experience in fast-paced, complex organizations (enterprise SaaS or technology experience highly preferred).

• While deep day-one expertise in Government Affairs, ESG or Philanthropy is not strictly required, you must possess a demonstrated ability and passion for championing policy, cultural, brand, and social impact functions.

• Senior-level financial oversight experience, including managing large operating and/or philanthropic budgets.

Competencies

• Commercial Acumen: A deep understanding of how public policy, sustainability, and social impact directly drive revenue and mitigate enterprise risk.

• Storytelling & Advocacy: Exceptional communicator and storyteller, with proven external speaking and public advocacy experience in high stakes settings.

• Leadership Presence: Calm, grounded leadership presence with the ability to influence C-level executives and the Board of Directors.

• Systems Thinking: Strong systems thinking and the ability to manage ambiguity with confidence, uniting disparate functions into a cohesive strategy.

• Talent Development: A track record of empowering seasoned domain experts while providing the executive air cover they need to scale their impact.

Bonus Skills

• Experience in cybersecurity, identity, trust, or AI governance.

• Existing relationships with key policymakers, regulators, and industry coalitions relevant to Okta’s business.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Scientists use Claude across the life sciences, from drug discovery and research biology to clinical development and manufacturing. To support that work, Anthropic introduced the Life Sciences Verification Program (LSVP), which gives verified life science professionals access to Claude with a refined set of safeguards that is more permissive for biology-related work. The program is in beta.We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own the program of work that expands that access and helps scale it with safety in mind.

Each expansion depends on many teams at once and no single team owns the path end to end. You'll become the single owner of that program, the person who knows what each expansion requires, where every workstream stands, what it is waiting on, and who needs to decide. This is a cross-org execution role, not a research role, and it does not require a life sciences background. LSVP is the starting point, and the scope will grow alongside Anthropic's broader work in the life sciences. Over time, more of the life sciences community can get verified access, and each new expansion takes less bespoke effort than the last.

Responsibilities

• Own the program for expanding access to Anthropic's life sciences verification programs: scoping, sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs across safeguards, platform, and product engineering teams

• Scope and drive the cross-org engineering work that each expansion requires, from new plan and account types to new platforms

• Partner with the product manager to turn program goals into a sequenced plan with clear owners and dates

• Drive clarity on data access, retention, and review requirements, and on the changes they require across safeguards, access, and provisioning

• Drive user experience scoping across the Claude product surfaces where the program is available

• Find and remove the technical blockers that keep eligible organizations from accessing life sciences capabilities

• Establish the operating rhythm: a single view of workstreams, owners, dependencies, risks, and status, with planning, escalation paths, and launch coordination across orgs

• Convert recurring efforts into documented, repeatable processes so that each new expansion requires less bespoke coordination

You may be a good fit if you

• Have several years of experience in technical program management, with a track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs

• Have experience coordinating across multiple engineering teams and organizations simultaneously, including safeguards, platform, and product partners

• Can engage meaningfully with the engineers doing the work, from platform and access systems to product surfaces

• Are highly organized and can manage multiple parallel workstreams effectively across distributed teams

• Thrive in unstructured environments with a knack for bringing order to chaos and creating clarity in ambiguous situations

• Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority

• Have worked on cloud or platform programs (preferred but not required)

• Do not need a life sciences background. This is not a research role, and no life sciences experience is required

• Are passionate about Anthropic's mission and interested in the challenges of bringing AI capabilities to the life sciences community safely and reliably

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$290,000 — $365,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. About the Role
Lead OpenAI’s site network infrastructure delivery, coordinating the physical installation and readiness of network systems with the central network team and contracted installation providers.
You will be OpenAI’s accountable on-site lead for physical network infrastructure construction and deployment, directing and overseeing the work of general contractors, specialist contractors and other service providers within your discipline. You will combine practical subject-matter depth with hands-on field leadership, managing contracted support to deliver safe, high-quality work to the integrated construction plan.
Reporting and scope
Report to the Site Construction Manager, who reports through the applicable project-management leadership. Maintain functional alignment with the Network Infrastructure leader and central network engineering team.
Own day-to-day discipline execution and contractor performance within the assigned site scope and delegated authority. Coordinate priorities and interfaces through the Site Construction Manager; escalate material cost, schedule, design and acceptance decisions to the appropriate owners.
This is a senior site delivery role, suited to an experienced superintendent, supervisor, manager or trade lead. Accountability is for an assigned discipline and site work packages. Site assignment, duration and any shared coverage follow project phase, workload and the staffing plan; effective on-site coverage is required during critical activities.
Key Responsibilities
• Manage structured-cabling contractors, fiber installers, network installation partners and other service providers against the site delivery plan.

• Translate approved network designs into executable field packages and coordinate bills of materials, material availability and installation sequencing with the central network team.

• Oversee pathways, duct banks and building-entry interfaces, fiber and copper cabling, racks, patching, labeling and network-equipment installation as applicable.

• Direct fiber and cabling quality assurance, review test results and traceability, and drive correction of defective or incomplete installations.

• Coordinate power, cooling, space and physical access readiness with electrical, mechanical and CSLA leads and hardware deployment teams.

• Coordinate network provisioning, connectivity validation and handover with authorized network engineering and operations teams; maintain accurate installation and as-built records.

• Set clear contractor deliverables and work priorities; review staffing, progress and quality, identify constraints early, and drive recovery actions through the Site Construction Manager.

• Provide concise progress and risk reporting, evaluate field impacts of proposed changes, and maintain accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams.

Qualifications
• Typically 8–10 years of large-scale data center network deployment, structured cabling, physical-layer installation or infrastructure delivery, with demonstrated field and contractor leadership. Equivalent depth of practical delivery experience will be considered.

• Strong understanding of physical data center network topologies, network components, bills of materials, rack constraints and installation sequencing; translate approved designs into executable field plans.

• Deep practical knowledge of fiber and copper plant installation, trunks, panels, terminations, cleaning, labeling and cable administration, including routing diversity and pathway separation.

• Ability to oversee and assess port-to-port verification, continuity, optical power and optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) testing; troubleshoot field installation and mapping discrepancies and verify remediation.

• Experience defining contractor work packages and statements of work, evaluating delivery requirements, forecasting labor needs and tracking quality, throughput, cost drivers and schedule performance within delegated authority.

• Experience coordinating deployment prerequisites with engineering and construction teams and completing formal operations handover with as-builts, port maps, test evidence and clear ownership transfer.

• Comfort with ticket-based execution, change control, incident escalation and documentation workflows that make network installation repeatable and auditable.

• Demonstrated ability to lead contractors and service providers through changing site conditions, set clear deliverables and acceptance criteria, and resolve performance gaps across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority.

• Strong written and verbal communication: maintain accurate field records, action and decision logs, and explain technical risks, schedule impacts and recovery options to site leadership, engineers and delivery partners.

• Sound judgment when information is incomplete: identify assumptions, prerequisites and interfaces, determine what work can proceed within approved authority, and escalate unresolved risks before they affect safety, quality or delivery.

• Relevant trade, apprenticeship, technical or degree-based preparation, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated field leadership and subject-matter competence are central to this site role.
